sources.citation: Triandaphyllidis, Manolis A. 1924. Eine zigeunerisch-griechische Geheimsprache. Zeitschrift für vergleichende Sprachforschung 52(1/2): 1-42.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist/etymological study of Dortika (Karpenisi, Kerasovo). §7 'Lautliches' (pp. 27-29) gives no stress-placement rule; it only notes that Romani o/e 'in unbetonter Silbe' are raised to u/i as in northern Greek (p. 27) and, in glossary entries, that the Greek-side accent of ἀνανάι already matches Romani nanái (p. 7), an 'oxytonierte Form' matchó (p. 11), and 'die Akzentverschiebung nach ψείρα' in τζούβα (p. 16). Dortika forms are printed in Greek orthography with accents, but no general statement of where stress falls.
Tertiary; no phonology or stress information; names Dortika and Kaliarda as 'dialects' and cites Ethnologue, Bakker & Mous 1994, Matras & Bakker 2003, Nicholas 2017.

sources.citation: Hancock, Ian F. 2021. Para-Romani in Scandinavia. East European Journal of Psycholinguistics 8(2). DOI 10.29038/eejpl.2021.8.2.han.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Cites Sechidou 2005 in its bibliography; the only stress remark is 'English stress-placement' for an Angloromani word (p. 73 fn. 2). Nothing on Greek Para-Romani.
Lists Sechidou 2005, Triandaphyllidis 1924, Matras 2002: 242-249, Ethnologue; alternative names Hellenoromani, Romika. No linguistic content.
